transcript:
This is NPR News now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
The Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade in New York City has been postponed until Saturday
as a coastal storm moves up the east coast with heavy rain and strong gusty winds.
The city is under a high wind warning.
Organizers say they made the decision out of an abundance of caution for the marchers,
floats, and giant balloon handlers.
Will Koss is executive producer of the parade.
Since 1924, the parade has continued to march down the streets of New York City.
We're a rain or shine event.
We don't even postponed for three years during World War II, and that was an opportunity
for us to donate some of our materials to the war effort.
So this was an unprecedented situation.
Speaking there on NPR's Morning Edition.
Almost 60% of holiday shoppers plan to use AI this weekend for help, according to the
National Retail Federation.
New AI agents are designed to handle shopping tasks like comparing prices across websites
and can even do actual buying.
But NPR's Stephen Bissaha says users should be careful how much private data they hand
over to AI.
AI agents can do more than shopping to make the holidays easier.
Like keeping an eye on all your incoming packages through your mail.
Even contact a seller for you if something goes wrong.
Pretty useful.
Sure, but you can't tell it not to look at all of your other email either.
Emily Pfeiffer of Forrester advises retailers about AI commerce.
There are so many horror stories out there about the ways that they're sort of misfiring
and doing things that put consumer data at risk.
Like users reporting agents sending emails or even using a credit card to book a hotel
all without permission.
Pfeiffer says it is okay to use AI for finding gifts, but recommend shoppers do the buying
themselves.
Stephen Bissaha, NPR News.
The former head of the lead U.S. aid agency is calling on Congress to investigate what
she calls the reckless release of internal documents for political purposes.
Samantha Power made the comment after the Trump administration used the USAID website
to post some of her former emails, as NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports.
When the Trump administration dismantled the U.S. Agency for International Development,
it also erased information on the website, detailing decades of American aid work.
Now it has posted internal memos about contacts with social media organizations.
The Trump administration says this shows that the agency was weaponized against the American
people.
Former USAID administrator Samantha Power says it shows her staff working transparently
on tasks including countering Chinese disinformation.
She says the incoming Congress should restore the website to let Americans see the full
picture, not this "baffling hodgepodge chosen by people who don't take responsibility for
their lethal mistakes."
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, Washington.
In Eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, the fast-moving Ebola outbreak has now topped
12,000 confirmed cases, and the country's Ministry of Health says nearly half of them
have died.
This says fighting between rebels and the army is hampering efforts to contain the disease,
which is the fastest-growing outbreak in history.
The World Health Organization says the fighting has prevented teams from reaching some communities
and left some treatment centers with fewer staff.
Duran Duran's original guitarist Andy Taylor has died following a bout with prostate cancer.
NPR's Isabella Gomez-Sarmiento says Taylor and the British band first made their mark
on pop-rock music during the 1980s.
The year was 1980, and the ad in Melody Maker Music magazine sought out a "live-wire guitarist"
for a band.
A young Eddie Taylor auditions for the gig, and just a few years later, the music of Duran
Duran would become a global sensation.
Duran Duran became a fixture of the newly formed MTV, and their new wave synth-heavy
sound became a staple of the 80s.
Andy Taylor and his bandmates parted ways later that decade, though they would reunite
years later.
By 2022, Taylor was too sick to join Duran Duran for its Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction,
but in a shared statement, his bandmates wrote of his remarkable courage, honesty, and grace.
Isabella Gomez-Sarmiento, NPR News.
And I'm Janine Herbst, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
